title: Code Factory: Proof-by-Sabotage Software Factory
description:
Code Factory is a proof-first, open-source software factory for turning specifications, behavior checks, design contracts, policy verification, and release receipts into auditable delivery. Version 0.31 adds the Native E2E Proof Gate and Team Pilot readiness: an approved positive/negative command-pair gate records HOLLOW_E2E_TEST when the declared negative path unexpectedly succeeds; a separate local readiness gate hash-binds five non-secret operating decisions for up to three human-selected, customer-managed reference partners. Neither command provisions infrastructure, enrolls a customer, accepts payment, activates a service, or claims managed availability. Plan-to-Proof Review continues to compare a strict, human-approved agent plan with exact changed paths, declared test paths, review tiers, and existing Diff-to-Proof facts. It writes explicit Proof Debt for scope drift, missing declared tests, required deep-review routing, and source claims without proof. Unified Graph Ops remains a deterministic, read-only view over local Product, Mission, Proof, Gate, Trace, receipt, and artifact facts. Public evidence includes Mermaid diagrams, the current FactoryLine identity asset, and actual product captures.

Evidence boundary: all proof commands are local, deterministic, and bounded to declared inputs. They do not execute unapproved shell strings, read AI transcripts, call a provider, approve, merge, publish, deploy, sign, or claim readiness. Graph Ops is bounded to readable local artifacts and does not claim time, token, cost, productivity, or conversion savings. The optional GitHub workflow is limited to read contents plus scoped pull-request comment and Check publication, ignores fork pull requests, and never uses pull_request_target. A passing receipt proves the declared checks and supplied environment, not arbitrary production security.
